issues.failure_explanation:
The declared periodic spaces $\mathcal V=H^1_{\mathrm{per}}(\Omega)^2$, $\mathcal C=H^1_{\mathrm{per}}(\Omega)^2$ contain nonzero constants, for which $\lVert\mathbf v_hVert>0=\lVert
abla\mathbf v_hVert$; the asserted Poincaré inequality 'for all $\mathbf v_h\in\mathcal V_h$ and $\mathbf C_h\in\mathcal C_h$' is therefore false as quantified. The paper concedes the estimate holds only on the zero-mean subspace, but zero mean is assumed only for the exact solution (Assumption ef{assu:regularity}); it is not enforced on $\mathcal V_h,\mathcal C_h$ and is not preserved by the scheme (testing eq:fully_B1 with a constant shows the discrete mean of $\mathbf B_h$ is driven by terms containing $
abla\cdot\mathbf u_h$, $
abla\cdot\mathbf B_h$, which do not vanish). Hence the stability proof's estimate of $|\langle\mathbf f^n,\mathbf u_h^nangle|+|\langle\mathbf g^n,\mathbf B_h^nangle|$ via $\lVert\mathbf u_h^nVert_{H^1}\le C\lVert
abla\mathbf u_h^nVert$, and the Poincaré/Ladyzhenskaya estimates applied to $\xi_{\mathbf u}^n,\xi_{\mathbf B}^n,\psi_{\mathbf u}^n,\psi_{\mathbf B}^n$ in the convergence proof, are unjustified for periodic boundary conditions.

\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the periodic spaces $\mathcal V,\mathcal C,\mathcal V_h,\mathcal C_h$ (and the projectors) to zero spatial mean and verify the trilinear identities and well-posedness on that subspace, and additionally control the constant mode of the scheme as defined (its mean drifts through the $\ell$-terms); or restate Theorems thm:stability and thm:convergence for homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions only.
issues.overall_effect: The stability inequality of Theorem thm:stability and the convergence estimate of Theorem thm:convergence are unproved in the periodic case, which is part of the stated scope (case (ii) of the model) and the setting of the periodic vortex benchmarks.
issues.title: Poincaré inequality asserted for all discrete functions fails in the periodic case; mean mode uncontrolled
issues.why_classification: Every repair must either supply a contained but genuine argument bounding the uncontrolled constant mode of the periodic scheme, or drop the periodic regime from the theorems' scope; not a local one-line fix, but no new global architecture and a comparable result survives, so not serious.

issues.why_classification: A short, standard local repair (inf-sup assumption plus one projection estimate and two Young inequalities) preserves the statement, rate, and scope of Theorem thm:convergence.

issues.failure_explanation:
In the proof of Theorem thm:convergence the residual terms are bounded by $C(\lVert\mathbf r_1^nVert^2+\lVert\mathbf r_2^nVert^2)$ and then folded into $I_2$ and $R=C(h^{2l}+h^{2m}+	au^2)$, which requires $\|\mathbf r_1^n\|+\|\mathbf r_2^n\|\le C	au$. No such bound is proved in the paper. The cited formula eq:frac_replacement asserts $O(	au)$ accuracy under the sole condition $0<
u(t_n)<1$, with no regularity of $\phi$ or of $
u$; for the MHD solution this estimate needs second-order time regularity ($\partial_{tt}\mathbf u$, $\partial_{tt}\mathbf B$) and time-regularity of the order functions (e.g. Lipschitz continuity of $
u(t)$), none of which follows from Assumption ef{assu:regularity} (only $\partial_t\mathbf u,\partial_t\mathbf B\in L^\infty H^{l+1}$) or Assumption ef{assu:orders_bounds} (only $\alpha, eta\in C[0,T]$). The premise the proof relies on is therefore false or unestablished as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumptions \ref{assu:regularity}–\ref{assu:orders_bounds} by the standard hypotheses under which the variable-order L1 truncation bound holds (e.g. $\partial_{tt}\mathbf u,\partial_{tt}\mathbf B\in L^\infty(0,T;L^2(\Omega)^2)$ and $\alpha,\beta$ Lipschitz), and state/prove (or cite with hypotheses verified) $\|\mathbf r_i^n\|\le C\tau$ before using it.
issues.overall_effect: The first-order-in-time convergence guarantee of Theorem thm:convergence is unsupported; the error term contributed by the L1 truncation is unbounded under the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: Convergence proof needs O(τ) L1 truncation bounds that the stated assumptions do not support
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard regularity assumptions and the standard truncation lemma is a local, routine repair; the theorem's statement, rate, and scope all survive unchanged.
